issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch: The problem statement and UML require a SealSaloon constructor that accepts a String (saloon name). The reference solution implements a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()). This discrepancy will confuse students about the required constructor signature and what to implement.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the constructor signatures consistent. Either update the solution/template to provide SealSaloon(String name) (and store the name if intended), or update the problem statement and UML to require a no-argument constructor. Preferable fix: implement public SealSaloon(String name) in the solution/template to match the problem/UML or change the specification to explicitly state a no-arg constructor if the name is not needed.

issues.description: Inconsistent specification about the stock attribute: the problem text first describes a final Stock stock that should be initialized in the constructor (instance field), but later explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static and shared across instances. The reference solution uses a static final stock initialized at declaration. This contradiction (instance final initialized in constructor vs. static shared field) is structural and will confuse students about whether stock should be an instance field or a static shared field and where/how to initialize it.
issues.suggested_fix: Clarify and make consistent whether stock is an instance (final) field initialized in the constructor or a static shared field. If the intent is a shared stock across all saloons, update the earlier wording to state 'static final Stock stock' (and show initialization at declaration or in a static initializer). If the intent is an instance-level final stock, remove the instruction that stock must be static and update the solution to initialize stock in the constructor (non-static). Ensure the UML and all textual instructions reflect the same choice.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies a constructor SealSaloon(String) that takes a saloon name, while both the template (Main.java) and the reference solution implement and call a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). This mismatch between the required constructor signature in the problem description and the constructors used in the code artifacts can confuse students about which constructor they must implement and how to instantiate SealSaloon.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and UML to require a no-argument constructor SealSaloon() (and remove the text that claims a name parameter is required), or (B) add a matching constructor SealSaloon(String name) to the template and solution (and update the Main calls accordingly). Choose the option that matches the intended tests; if both constructors are acceptable, document that a no-arg constructor or an overload accepting String is allowed.
